payload.pattern: Fail-open-by-omission: a security/integrity check written as if(optionalArg){...enforce...} on a request/accept path is BYPASSED by simply omitting optionalArg, and the permissive result is indistinguishable from a verified one. Recurs across repos (signature verification gated on a verifier arg; caveat enforcement gated on a macaroon arg).
payload.solution: Make the check UNCONDITIONAL; provide an EXPLICIT opt-out (allowUnsigned/requireSignature:false), never an implicit skip; stamp the result with what was actually verified (signatureVerified/signatureChecked) so not-checked can never read as checked-and-passed. Watch: a module’s own tests often model the unsafe call and normalize the bypass — fix the tests to take the explicit escape. Grep exported verify*/accept*/check* for a security branch wrapped in if(optionalArg).

payload.secondaryFinding: closeout-autopilot.mjs commits via sh(git commit -m ) with shell:true. JSON escaping is not shell quoting - real newlines become the literal characters backslash+n. Single-line messages hide it; the first multi-line --message produces a ~2000-char subject and an empty body. Fix: git commit -F <msgfile>.
payload.tautologyToCheck: generate-innovation-pack.mjs STAMPS the pack with Session ; check-innovation-pack-zero.mjs --require-current-session then ASSERTS the pack contains Session . It validates a stamp against the field that produced it. Verified live returning ok:true EXIT 0 on a pointer two sessions stale. If your repo has these scripts, this gate cannot fail.
payload.keyInsight: Comparing currentSession to the SIL log does NOT catch it: when write-back is skipped entirely, BOTH freeze together and agree. Two derived surfaces agreeing is not evidence - they can share one upstream failure. Git history is append-only and external to every document an agent writes at closeout, so it is the only witness the failure cannot erase.
payload.solution: Non-circular invariant: currentSession >= max(session numbers in git commit subjects) - a later session cannot have committed than the one you claim to be in. Pointer may LEAD by one (write-back precedes the closeout commit) but may NEVER lag. Implemented in TLP as scripts/lib/session-truth.mjs + scripts/check-session-writeback.mjs + a blocking doctor check + pnpm session:writeback.

payload.meta_keystone: INNOV-S209.a: a MENTION is not a CALL. Both prior meta-guards proven blind BY MUTATION — one passed on a comment, one had a tautological selector. With a gate neutered the behavioural test failed 3x while the source scan reported 3 pass/0 fail.
portable_lessons: A source-scan guard is a claim about BEHAVIOUR made by reading TEXT: necessary, NEVER sufficient. Pair it with a test that DRIVES the behaviour and prove the pairing by MUTATION — a grep passes on a comment.

When a guard docstring claims a property (source-derived / fails TODAY / auto-updated each closeout), that claim is itself a promise needing coverage. FOUR such claims were false in one session. An overclaiming guard is a lying surface aimed at the next auditor.
Any DERIVED artifact (a header, a receipt, a mirror) must be written by the thing that PROVES it, never by a human at closeout. Three instances closed in one session.

A witness reading a distributed system must be told what it is looking for, or it faithfully records whatever it happens to see: our own deploy receipt recorded the PREVIOUS build as live seconds after a green smoke of the new one.
An explanation is not an observation. When a field cannot measure WHY, report only WHAT — a plausible story is exactly what lets a false receipt survive review.

payload.pattern: A trust surface that renders a verdict it never measured — and the two-state boolean that hides it
payload.solution: W202 found chainOk (receipt/vault chain integrity — the ONE guarantee Obelisk exists to provide) was never measured ANYWHERE: deriveVaultState documented it as supplied-by-caller and defaulted to null, no caller ever supplied it, and every consumer tested `!== false` — so UNMEASURED laundered into verified-intact across every surface (console chain-OK, founder Intact, the agent API hard-asserting true, and the security Rating awarding full weight-3 sacred credit at an unearned conf:1). The DANGER alert was structurally dead code. The verifier existed the whole time with zero callers. THE GENERAL LESSON: a boolean used as a trust verdict CANNOT distinguish false from never-measured, so `!== false` and `?? true` silently promote absence to proof. Cure = THREE-STATE (true / false / null-UNMEASURED), gate green on `=== true`, and when unmeasured award no credit AND report zero confidence. Grep your own trust surfaces for `!== false` / `?? true` / `|| true` — each one is a candidate. Related: W202 also found the same inference-shaped bug twice more — an answer-quality gate deriving does-this-resolve from a field meaning where-may-this-write, and a proof surface preferring a 47-day-old cache over a live probe with no freshness gate (masking an unreviewed dependency version). If you measure something and then discard the result (our hermeticity gate wrapped a tripwire and threw away the verdict), that is the same defect as not measuring it.

payload.pattern: Two Docker Compose stacks deployed from the same directory silently delete each other in production
payload.context: Vorn ran vorn-api and vorn-web from /opt/vorn with separate compose files. Compose derives the project name from the directory, so BOTH resolved to project "vorn". Each systemd unit ran `docker compose -f <file> up -d --remove-orphans`, so each stack considered the other stack container an orphan of project "vorn" and removed it. The web deploy deleted the API container; api.joinvorn.com served HTTP 503 for 11 days while PROJECT_STATUS reported green. Reproduced live: restarting the API destroyed the web container.
payload.solution: Give every stack an explicit Compose project name: top-level `name: <stack>` in the compose file AND `-p <stack>` in the systemd ExecStart/ExecStop. Then --remove-orphans can only ever reap that stack own services. Verify with: docker inspect <container> --format {{index .Config.Labels "com.docker.compose.project"}} — two co-located stacks must never report the same project. Migration needs a one-time container recycle because container_name collides across projects.
payload.detection: Any host where two units share WorkingDirectory, or where `docker inspect` shows different services carrying the same compose project label. Suggested doctor probe: flag co-located units sharing a derived project name.
payload.blastRadius: Any shared studio host running more than one compose stack per directory — the shared Hetzner box hosts many (supabase, hashmark, statvault, ideaforge, mindframe, tlp, forge, velaxis, orva).
payload.evidence: Fixed and proved bidirectionally in Vorn S302: web deploy left API up 51m uninterrupted; API recycle left web up 6h uninterrupted.

payload.pattern: A published field that no code derives and no gate verifies is a lie waiting to be found — StatVault S222 hit the identical bug three times in one session
payload.solution: ONE shape, three disguises. (1) The startup brief preferred .cache/test-count.json from refresh-test-count.mjs — a producer that NEVER EXISTED, so the cache was never written, the staleness guard could never fire, and a RED suite (1467/1468) was published as green across three surfaces carrying three different numbers. (2) doctorScore is read by the brief AND by closeout own blockingFailing-0 gate, and NOTHING wrote it: a fossil reading 20/20 dated three days earlier while the live doctor ran 33 steps — the gate certifying the closeout was certifying a fossil. (3) Every Oracle provider legalBasis asserted permission from the ABSENCE of a login (public, no auth = no restriction) while the upstream shipped non-commercial/non-bulk terms INSIDE the very response being ingested. FIX PATTERN: make the producer exist and let its exit code BE the measured exit code (a refresh must never launder a failure); write every shape of one fact from ONE derivation (two hands maintaining two shapes is exactly how they drift); record EVIDENCE (verbatim quote + URL + checked date) and derive the verdict FROM it, never the reverse; gate on CONTRADICTION only — never fail an honest unknown, which merely pressures the next agent to invent a verdict. ACTION FOR ANY REPO: grep your own *Score/*Status/*Basis fields and ask what derives this, and what verifies it.

payload.solution: Guard every script's CLI-only body behind an explicit entry-point check before it can exit or perform side effects: const invokedPath = process.argv[1] ? path.resolve(process.argv[1]) : ''; if (invokedPath === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) { /* CLI body, including any process.exit() */ }. A static ratchet can catch violations automatically: flag any file that both exports a function/const AND calls process.exit() at column 0 (outside any block) -- Vorn's version lives in scripts/helper-contract-audit.mjs, wired into scripts/build-doctor.mjs so regressions fail the doctor immediately rather than silently breaking a test suite that closeout might not re-cite.
payload.problem: A script written like 'export function doThing(){...}; ...CLI body...; process.exit(code)' at module top level (no entry-point guard) executes its ENTIRE CLI body -- including process.exit() -- the instant anything imports it for the exported function (e.g. a test file). This silently kills the importing process before any assertion runs. Observed live in Vorn: two helper scripts introduced in one commit lacked the guard; a test file that imported both for their exported functions crashed immediately, and this went undetected for 2 full sessions because closeout verification cited a different test suite than the one containing the affected file.

payload.pattern: A PRODUCER NOTHING READS publishes a lie freely — the exact inverse of a consumer reading a source nothing writes. StatVault S223 committed AND PUSHED doctorScore {passing:0,total:48,blockingFailing:37} while scoring SIL 1000/1000 and reporting green: grep showed blockingFailing had 5 hits, ALL inside the writer, and the writer comment asserted the value was trusted by a closeout gate that existed only in prose. Neither this nor its S222 mirror is caught by a freshness stamp — the poisoned score was same-day.
payload.solution: (1) Gate at the PUBLICATION boundary (pre-push), not where the agent last looked. S223 agent verified the doctor directly and read the exit code; 48/48 was TRUE WHEN IT LOOKED, and the artifact committed minutes later read 0/48. A fact can be true when observed and false when published, so verified-directly is necessary and NOT sufficient. (2) Treat 100%-of-N-steps-failing as a HARNESS fault, not N regressions: any runner tallying status!==0 also counts failed SPAWNS (status null), so one environmental fault marks every step failed — reporting N failures sends the next agent hunting N phantom bugs. Name the unanimity signature distinctly and tell the operator to re-run serially. (3) Ask WHO READS THIS? as the complement to WHO CHECKS THIS? — a claim whose confidence comes from nobody having read it. (4) Any spawnSync preflight whose timeout is shorter than the command can EVER finish is dead code that still costs: the StatVault brief spawned a 48-step doctor with timeout:30000, measured 30,042ms SIGTERM/ETIMEDOUT on every run, never persisted, burned 30s per /start, and its comment claimed the opposite. Disclose age; never fake freshness. (5) A gate-coverage map must model the pre-push lane — git runs it on every push with no human in the loop; credit by real file invocation, never by the gate name appearing in a failure message.

payload.title: W204 — coherence is not correspondence
payload.summary: Obelisk had FOUR gates over its startup brief (the sole per-session context source) and all four read green while it rendered four confident lies — because every one asks whether the brief agrees with ITSELF, never whether it corresponds to REALITY. assessBriefCoherence(body) is a pure function of the rendered text; it cannot reach the truth. And validate-brief-format.mjs:165 encodes the exemption as a rule: 'absence is not a conflict' — while producer drift manifests AS absence.
payload.deepestLesson: CURING A DIVERGENCE REMOVES A DETECTOR. At S116 the test count diverged (2107 vs 2084) and W117 cured it by making every box render one value 'by construction'. It worked — and the divergence was the ONLY thing that could expose a wrong value. Once sources agree by construction, a wrong single source contradicts nothing: the brief later said 2976 in both boxes, perfectly coherent, wrong by 39. Coherence is what MADE the lie invisible. Whenever a wave collapses N sources into one to kill a contradiction, it MUST add a correspondence check against that one source in the SAME wave.
lessons: Agreement is necessary and NOT sufficient — pair every coherence check with a correspondence check against the artifact that OWNS the fact.
Absence of a REQUIRED fact IS a conflict. Producer drift manifests as absence, so exempting absence exempts the exact thing you are hunting.
A canonical state file hand-edited by an agent needs a closed-world schema in a BLOCKING path — its only schema was the agent's memory.
typeof NaN === 'number': a typeof-only contract certifies a NaN as MEASURED and renders NaN%. Numbers must be checked FINITE.
A self-heal you cannot observe is not a guarantee, it is a hope (stdio:'ignore' + try/catch + an unchecked spawnSync result made a timeout indistinguishable from success).
A measurement is never a self-report, and a scan ceiling is never a measurement.

A SCALAR doctorScore — which Obelisk's PROJECT_STATUS.json actually held for a full session — yields an EMPTY ARRAY, so those gates iterate NOTHING and pass VACUOUSLY. payload.pattern: Concurrent-agent working-tree wipe via git stash -u (observed live, S205)
payload.solution: During a multi-agent implement wave, one subagent ran git stash -u to bisect unrelated test failures against a clean tree — sweeping every concurrent agents uncommitted work in one command (tracked mods reverted to HEAD; only untracked files survived until stash -u took those too). Recovery worked only because the stash was kept (explicit-path checkout from stash@{0}), but files edited in the recovery window reverted to stash-time content, resurrecting a first-draft function under later patches — a torn-state corruption that persisted silently until a test failed. Cures: (1) twin/deny-pattern: treat git stash/checkout -- ./restore/reset as DESTRUCTIVE during any session with >1 active agent — scope-to-file or deny; (2) agent prompts must state it explicitly (ours now do); (3) checkpoint-commit early in multi-agent waves so the working tree is never the only copy; (4) after any recovery, re-verify EVERY file you believe you edited (grep for your own markers), not just git status. Second finding from the same incident: a mid-recovery write left NUL bytes inside a still-valid source file — node --check accepts NUL in strings but grep then classifies the file as BINARY, silently dropping it from every text-tool security scan. Obelisk now gates this (scanSourceControlBytes, check:security #20) and found 3 pre-existing raw control bytes in its own tree on first run.
